writeup: TIC 318620649 is a candidate eclipsing binary star detected through automated analysis of TESS photometry. The system shows a primary eclipse with a depth of 0.92% and an orbital period of 27.67 days, along with a secondary eclipse detected at 7.0 sigma significance. The detection achieved a strong signal-to-noise ratio of 60.8 in the Box Least Squares search, and pixel-level image analysis confirmed the source location near the target with a peak signal-to-noise of 7.3. The target does not appear in any of six major variable-star catalogs. However, data quality checks reveal that alternating eclipses differ significantly in depth, suggesting the initially measured period may have been underestimated - the corrected orbital period of 27.67 days accounts for this pattern.
